sections.content:
Interesting! The batch executed only 8 actions: LEFT×4, DOWN×4 (not 7). The player is now at (32,14) — rows 32–36, columns 14–18. And importantly, the red terminal block (rows 38–42, columns 19–22) is still there, and the player is right above it. Wait, why did the batch stop after 8 actions? The result shows board_changed True, done False. Maybe the 9th action (the 5th DOWN) was invalid/blocked, so the environment stopped the batch? The player is at (32,14); the next DOWN → (38,14): rows 38–42, columns 14–18 — that's black (the red block is at columns 19–22). It should be valid, but…
Hmm, wait, let me check: did the 5th DOWN actually execute and get blocked? The player is at (32,14). If DOWN had been executed and blocked, the player would stay at (32,14). The batch was supposed to be 16 actions, but only 8 were executed. So the environment halted the batch — probably because the 9th action was invalid (no movement) and the batch aborted.
Why would DOWN from (32,14) to (38,14) be invalid? Let me check the cells at rows 38–42, columns 14–18 in the current frame. From the ascii slice earlier: rows 38–42, columns 14–18 were 'BBBBBB' (black). Hmm, that was before this batch. Let me recheck the current frame.
Wait — maybe the player's jump passes through intermediate cells, and the red block at rows 38–42, columns 19–22 is… no, columns 14–18 don't include 19–22.
Hold on, maybe the movement isn't a fixed 6-cell jump but "slide until hitting a wall" — from (32,14), DOWN: the player slides down until it hits something. Below the player: rows 37 onward are black… the bottom of the maze is row 55. If it slides until hitting a wall, it should go to (50,14) (rows 50–54, the bottom corridor; row 55 is the maze's bottom edge?). Hmm, but in that case, the earlier moves: from (8,14) DOWN → should slide all the way to (50,14), not (14,14). But the history showed the player moved 6 at a time: (8,14)→(14,14)→(20,14)→(26,14)→(32,14). So it's a fixed 6-cell jump, and the 5th DOWN was blocked.
Let me look at the current ascii around rows 36–44, columns 12–24 to see what's blocking. Maybe the red terminal block is actually at columns 14–18 in the current frame? In the image, the red block is displayed at rows 38–42, columns 14–18 (to the left of the horizontal red line at row 40). Hmm, in the image, the red block appears to be at columns 14–18, rows 38–42. But in my ascii slice, the RRRR was at columns 19–22. Let me look again: the slice was lines[r][12:24], so index 0 = column 12. Row 38: `WBBBBBBBRRRR` → index 0='W' (column 12), 1–7='B' (columns 13–19), 8–11='R' (columns 20–23). Wait: `WBBBBBBBRRRR` = W(12), B(13), B(14), B(15), B(16), B(17), B(18), B(19), R(20), R(21), R(22), R(23). So the red is at columns 20–23! Not 19–22. I miscounted. So the red terminal block is at rows 38–42, columns 20–23.
Then (38,14): rows 38–42, columns 14–18 — all black. Valid!
So why was the batch aborted at 8? Maybe the batch wasn't aborted — maybe the environment only allows up to 8 actions per call? "One action usually returns one frame, but a single action can produce a short multi-frame animation." The result said 8 actions were executed. Maybe there's a per-call cap on the number of actions (8?). The first batch was 3 (no problem), then 1, and this time 16 requested but only 8 executed.
So the cap is probably 8 actions per call. OK — I'll just split the remaining 8 moves (DOWN×3, RIGHT×5) into another call.
